sources.title: The Archaeology of the Early Tibetan Plateau
sources.note: Peer reviewed regional synthesis stressing uneven archaeological knowledge, varied subsistence, and limits on turning material culture into one identity.

sources.title: Climbing into the past: first Himalayan mummies discovered in Nepal
sources.note: Official Nepal archaeology publication on the Mebrak communal cave, radiocarbon dates, human and animal remains, textiles, and analytical methods.

sources.title: Survey and excavations in central Tibet
sources.note: University project account of Bangga, Yukang, Badong, seasonal corrals, dating, ceramic analysis, GIS, and survey limits.

sources.title: High-elevation sheep and goat provisioning on the Tibetan Plateau, 3000 to 2200 BP
sources.note: Peer reviewed isotope, architecture, crop, fauna, corral, water, fodder, and mobility evidence from Bangga.

sources.title: Fields Under the Hoof: plant cultivation of Bronze and Iron Age agropastoralists
sources.note: University dissertation using macrobotanical and stable isotope evidence to examine watering, manuring, labor, food, and ecological variation across western Tibetan sites.

sources.title: The transition to a barley-dominant cultivation system in Tibet
sources.note: University research profile for peer reviewed archaeobotanical work at Bangga, including its broad 1055 to 211 BCE range.

sources.title: Variation in mortuary practice on the early Tibetan Plateau and the High Himalayas
sources.note: Scholarly comparison of regional graves, Mebrak mortuary treatment, animals, platforms, textiles, beads, and interpretive variation.

sources.title: An Introduction to Archaeological Exploration and Methodology in Upper Tibet
sources.note: Austrian Academy publication reviewing Upper Tibetan sites, Mebrak communal burial, carved platforms, grave goods, and chronological cautions.

sources.title: The linguistic prehistory on the eastern Tibetan Plateau
sources.note: Multidisciplinary study treating language dispersal as a model with archaeological and palaeoclimate limits, not a direct label on pottery.

sources.title: Long-term prehistoric human occupation in Western Tibet: Xiada Co
sources.note: Peer reviewed excavation and survey showing both new regional evidence and the uneven state of archaeological coverage.

sources.title: Pastoralism as Institutions: Modeling the Pastoral Landscape in Tibet
sources.note: University dissertation combining survey, excavation, GIS, radiocarbon dating, ceramics, networks, and cautious institutional interpretation.

sources.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Reconstructing Early Population History in the High Himalayas of Nepal
sources.note: Peer reviewed synthesis of Mebrak and Kyang chronology, communal burial, genomes, isotopes, skeletal stress, trauma, adaptation, and exchange.

sources.title: 3600 years of human adaptation to drought intensification on the southern Tibetan Plateau
sources.note: Peer reviewed environmental record relating drought, cultivation, pastoral strategies, and settlement without collapsing all plateau communities.

sources.title: High lamb natural mortality versus specialized culling at Bangga
sources.note: Peer reviewed age-at-death study of Bangga sheep and goat remains, herd management, mortality, and analytical uncertainty.

sources.title: Reconsidering Tibet’s early Metal Age through recent copper and iron finds
sources.note: China Tibetology Research Center review of regional metal sequences, rare fourth-century BCE iron, exchange routes, and unresolved dating.

sources.title: Mustang archaeological mission
sources.note: French government archaeology account of fragmented research, cave burials, ceramics, survey, and the Kali Gandaki route.

sources.title: A cultural and environmental monograph on Mebrak
sources.note: Official Nepal publication reporting Mebrak demographics, subadults, dental health, stress, activity, and strong preservation limits.

sources.title: Cave archaeology in Mustang and the Mebrak child mummy
sources.note: Nepal Journals Online article locating a fourth-century BCE child mummy within Mustang cave research and conservation history.

sources.title: On the origins of Tibetan
sources.note: University repository study of Proto-Tibetan reconstruction, whose forms are scholarly hypotheses rather than ancient inscriptions.

sources.title: Proto-Languages
sources.note: Reference work explaining comparative reconstruction and why a proto-language is unattested rather than a written sample.

sources.title: Old Tibetan Documents Online
sources.note: University corpus of selected Old Tibetan texts from the seventh to twelfth centuries, far later than this card.

sources.title: The Tibetic Languages
sources.note: CNRS overview distinguishing historically attested Old Tibetan and later Tibetic diversity from prehistoric archaeological labels.

proposedOverrides.name: Proto-Tibetan Cultures
proposedOverrides.summary: A cautious archaeological guide to diverse plateau and Himalayan communities grouped under an anachronistic atlas umbrella from 400 to 323 BCE.
